newsitem.title: UK: London precious metals trade in narrow bands.
newsitem.headline: London precious metals trade in narrow bands.

text.p: Gold traded in a tight price range early on Wednesday but dealers said it may manage a slight bounce in the near term.
"The market is a bit bearish. But we're seeing some physical buying from the Far East this morning, which is propping up the price," one London-based dealer said.
Bullion fixed at $378.60 an ounce, compared to $378.20 on Tuesday afternoon and a London close of $378.20/$378.70.
Prices had slid lower in New York late on Tuesday, briefly touching the critical support level at $377.35.
Traders attributed the drop to the market's bearish interpretation of fresh news about the International Monetary Fund's proposed gold sales of five million ounces of gold.

IMF treasurer David Williams told a London conference late on Tuesday that if the sales went ahead, about 500,000 ounces of gold would be sold at a time, amounting to seven percent of daily market turnover.
But gold's recent staying power above the critical price level just above $377 an ounce suggested a bounce was likely, possibly as high as $381, another dealer noted.
Next week's expiry of over-the-counter options, which provide the right but not the obligation to buy or sell metal at a given "strike" price, may also help push up prices.
"It's a week till the OTC options expiry and there's some interest at $380, and so I wouldn't be suprised if we edge up towards there," a dealer said.
Overall, however, market sentiment remained bearish since last week's rally, which peaked just under $385, reversed amid heavy selling from gold producers and investment funds.
Rally attempts were expected to be capped by gold miners selling metal forward through the end of the year.
Silver was barely changed from Tuesday's London close, up just one cent at $4.89/$4.91.
"Silver is in much the same position as gold. It didn't go far yesterday and it's definitely still in range," a dealer said.

Prices were expected to consolidate in a well-worn $4.85-$5.00 price band for now, but historical price charts indicated silver's upwards momentum was waning, analysts said. Platinum was wedged in a tight range, up $0.25 at $383.75/$384.75, and eyeing gold and silver for direction.
